text: Code reviews are a vital practice in software development. In a code review, another developer carefully examines the code you have written before it is merged into the main project. The most immediate benefit is catching bugs early. It is much cheaper and faster to fix a mistake during review than to discover it later in testing or, worse, in production. However, the value goes far beyond finding errors. Reviews are a powerful tool for knowledge sharing. They allow team members to learn from each other’s techniques and to understand different parts of the codebase. This shared understanding means the team is not dependent on a single person. Most importantly, they elevate the overall quality of the team's work, as consistent feedback encourages clearer, more maintainable code for everyone.
